failures.title: ./omni cannot start on WSL: CRLF in the launcher shebang
failures.symptom: env: 'python3\r': No such file or directory / env: use -[v]S to pass options in shebang lines
failures.how_detected: running ./omni doctor and ./omni gate from WSL during REQ-022
failures.root_cause: The working-tree copy of omni had CRLF line endings, so the shebang named an interpreter called 'python3\r'. .gitattributes already declares eol=lf and the committed blob is LF; the checkout was written by a Windows tool before that rule applied, and git does not rewrite an unchanged file, so nothing flagged it.
failures.fix_summary: Converted the working copy to LF (no content change in git) and added a test that fails if the launcher or the scripts contain CR.
failures.prevention_notes: .gitattributes eol=lf plus a test that reads the bytes on disk; git status alone cannot show a stale CRLF working copy.

failures.title: omni graph build dead-ends on an externally-managed Python
failures.symptom: tree-sitter is not installed. Install it with: pip install ... -- and that pip install is refused (PEP 668 externally-managed-environment)
failures.how_detected: running a plain ./omni graph build on Debian with the system Python
failures.root_cause: The error message assumed pip install works in the interpreter running omni. On a PEP 668 system it does not, so the only instruction given was one the machine refuses, and no code path looked for a virtualenv that already had the packages.
failures.fix_summary: graph build now re-runs itself under ~/.venvs/omni-graph (or OMNI_GRAPH_PYTHON) when tree-sitter is missing and prints venv setup commands instead of a refused pip install.
failures.no_test_reason: The failing environment is a system Python with no tree-sitter; reproducing it in a test means altering the interpreter. Verified by hand with a plain ./omni graph build, the no-venv path and a failing OMNI_GRAPH_PYTHON.

failures.title: omni graph view prints a link Windows Chrome cannot open from WSL
failures.symptom: The 3D graph page did not open properly in Chrome: the printed URL was file:///mnt/c/... and --open used a Linux launcher
failures.how_detected: user report after opening the page from a WSL shell
failures.root_cause: The URL was built from the Linux path, which only the WSL side can resolve; the code was only exercised where the browser and the shell share a filesystem view, so the browser-on-Windows case was never tried.
failures.fix_summary: Detect WSL with wslpath -w, print the file:///C:/... URL and Windows path, and launch the Windows browser through cmd.exe.
failures.no_test_reason: Needs WSL and a Windows browser. The page itself was checked for JS errors at three window sizes in headless Chromium; a real Windows Chrome was not available.

failures.title: Viewer checkbox label shows a literal \u2264
failures.symptom: The label read 'name labels (when \u2264 200 nodes in view)' in the page
failures.how_detected: reviewing a headless screenshot of the regenerated viewer
failures.root_cause: A JavaScript-style escape was written into HTML text. Escapes are only decoded inside a JS string, so the browser printed the six characters as-is.
failures.fix_summary: Replaced the escape with the ≤ entity.
failures.prevention_notes: The test scans the markup portion of the template for backslash-u escapes.

failures.title: Test detection classed a production Java class as a test
failures.symptom: backend-junit listed AdminAuditLogEntry.java (src/main) as a test file, so it moved to the assurance layer
failures.how_detected: reading omni graph why output against STEP_App during REQ-022
failures.root_cause: The JUnit signal matched the text '@WebMvcTest' anywhere in a file, including a code comment, and content detection ignored where the file lives.
failures.fix_summary: Annotation signals must start a line, and content detection skips src/main paths.
failures.prevention_notes: Signals are anchored to line starts; the fixture keeps a comment that mentions a test annotation in production code.

failures.title: Commits were tied to another project's requirement
failures.symptom: omni_graph.py showed REQ-021 (STEP_App's Select layout fix) because a commit body said 'pulled OmniEngineering REQ-021'
failures.how_detected: reading omni graph why omni_graph.py against STEP_App
failures.root_cause: Requirement ids were read from the whole commit message. A body may cite an id from another project, and ids that also exist in this registry collide.
failures.fix_summary: The subject line is authoritative; the body is consulted only when the subject names no requirement, and changelog-derived ties prefer ids in the entry heading.
failures.prevention_notes: A fixture commit carries a foreign id in its body and the test asserts it is ignored.

failures.title: omni test add --command was rejected as an unknown command
failures.symptom: make_ai.py: error: Unknown command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
failures.how_detected: registering OmniEngineering's own test suite with the new CLI
failures.root_cause: The option --command stored its value in args.command, which is the same argparse destination the top-level subcommand uses, so the value replaced the subcommand name.
failures.fix_summary: The option now stores to run_command.
failures.prevention_notes: The CLI test passes --command through the real parser; option destinations must not reuse the subparser's dest names.

failures.title: A short requirement id matched inside a longer one
failures.symptom: PROJ-1 was recorded by a changelog line that only mentioned PROJ-12, PROJ-123 and PROJ-1-beta
failures.how_detected: the robustness test for foreign id formats
failures.root_cause: The id pattern was bounded against letters and digits but not against a hyphen followed by more text, so a prefix of another id matched.
failures.fix_summary: The pattern now refuses a following hyphen-and-alphanumeric as well.
failures.prevention_notes: Ids come from the registry and are matched exactly; the test mixes PROJ-1, PROJ-12, PROJ-123 and PROJ-1-beta.

failures.title: Graph build needs tree-sitter for every language including python; local runs silently masked this by auto-finding a venv
failures.symptom: CI's main test matrix (no [graph] extra, 6 OS/Python jobs) failed uniformly: FAIL: test_json_output_matches_the_direct_call and test_text_output_names_each_case (test_benchmark.TestBenchmarkCLI), FAIL: test_the_post_commit_hook_rebuilds_the_graph_in_the_background_without_blocking (test_gate_hook), all with 'Graph file not found' or 'the background build never produced a graph'
failures.how_detected: GitHub Actions CI (the workflow this same session added)
failures.root_cause: parse_python_file() calls load_language('python') unconditionally, so Python parsing has always gone through tree-sitter -- there is no stdlib-ast fallback anywhere in this codebase, despite build_graph()'s own stats defaulting the mode label to the literal string 'ast'. That mislabel, plus this development machine's ~/.venvs/omni-graph venv always being silently auto-detected and re-exec'd into by reexec_with_graph_python(), meant the true no-extras environment was never actually exercised locally -- only CI (a genuinely clean machine) exposed it.
failures.fix_summary: Fixed the misleading 'ast' stats label to 'tree-sitter'. Rewrote TestBenchmarkCLI's two failing tests to pass --graph at a hand-built fixture graph (same pattern as TestBenchmark) instead of invoking a real omni graph build, so they need no extra. Skipped the one test that must run a real build when tree-sitter is unavailable, and added a test-suite run to the graph-extra CI job (which does install the extra) so that skipped test is exercised there instead.
failures.prevention_notes: Reproduced locally by overriding HOME for the subprocess so ~/.venvs/omni-graph is not found, matching CI's real environment -- the only reliable way this machine can exercise the true no-extras path, since the auto-detection is silent by design.

failures.title: CI workflow YAML broke on an unquoted colon in a step name
failures.symptom: Push 9376171 failed instantly (0s) with 'This run likely failed because of a workflow file issue'
failures.how_detected: gh run view after the push; confirmed with python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)' locally
failures.root_cause: A step name, 'Run the test suite (with the [graph] extra: the tests skipped above run for real here)', contains an unquoted colon-space, which YAML parses as the start of a nested mapping rather than plain scalar text.
failures.fix_summary: Quoted the step name. Now validated with a local YAML parse before pushing a workflow change.
failures.no_test_reason: A dedicated regression test would need a YAML-parsing dependency (PyYAML), which this project's own test suite deliberately avoids to stay stdlib-only; PyYAML isn't guaranteed present on a fresh clone. Prevention is process instead: validate any workflow edit with a local YAML parse before pushing (now done for this fix and noted for next time).
failures.prevention_notes: Any GitHub Actions step name or other string value containing a colon needs quoting; run yaml.safe_load locally before pushing a workflow edit.

failures.title: The withdrawn status reached the CLI but not the schema; the failing test was misread as the known failure
failures.symptom: test_schema_enum_matches_the_cli_vocabulary failed on main since REQ-031: the schema enum lacked 'withdrawn' while REQUIREMENT_STATUSES had it.
failures.how_detected: full suite run before REQ-034, read by test name
failures.root_cause: The schema edit was overwritten in the working tree by a shell command that ran in the wrong directory before the REQ-031 commit, and every later suite run reported one failure, which was assumed to be the pre-existing hook test without checking the name.
failures.fix_summary: withdrawn restored in the enum; the existing test now passes.
failures.prevention_notes: Read a failing suite by test name, never by failure count; a known failure does not license ignoring the next one.

failures.title: Arbiter's own reports were committed and then gated: the output directory was not ignored before the first run
failures.symptom: On the arbiter branch every Python 3.12 CI cell failed omni gate: the completion.arbiter_gate command exited 1 with 10 new high findings, all authored.security-check-disabled, located in arbiter-out/check/report.json and arbiter-out/omni-gate/report.json.
failures.how_detected: CI run on the arbiter branch, reproduced locally with the analyzers removed from PATH
failures.root_cause: The branch wired Arbiter by hand before arbiter_install existed, ran arbiter check and arbiter gate, then committed with git add -A while .gitignore did not yet list arbiter-out/. Arbiter's --changed scan reads everything the diff touches, so the previous reports (whose finding titles quote the TLS-off patterns) became scan input and matched as new high findings. --out only excludes its own directory, not sibling runs under arbiter-out/.
failures.fix_summary: The two reports are untracked on the arbiter branch (git rm --cached); arbiter-out/ stays in .gitignore and in allowed_root_paths. arbiter_install already writes the ignore entry; the README now says a hand-wired workspace must do the same before its first run.
failures.no_test_reason: A repository-state defect (a committed output directory), not a code path: the fix is the untracking and the ignore entry, which git enforces from now on.
failures.prevention_notes: Ignore a tool's output directory before its first run, and review git add -A output for generated files; Arbiter reads its own reports as source if they are tracked.

failures.title: omni test run's timeout waited for the whole command on Windows
failures.symptom: tests/test_test_run.py::TestRunOneSuite::test_a_command_that_overruns_the_timeout_is_timeout_not_a_hang failed on both Windows CI cells: a 0.5 s timeout returned TIMEOUT after 30.03 s, the full sleep of the command.
failures.how_detected: CI on PR #2 (windows-latest, Python 3.10 and 3.12), read by test name
failures.root_cause: subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=...) kills only the shell it started; on Windows the child python process kept the inherited stdout and stderr pipes open, so communicate() blocked until the grandchild exited. The timeout therefore bounded nothing.
failures.fix_summary: run_test_suite starts the command in its own process group (CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP on Windows, start_new_session elsewhere) and on timeout kills the whole tree (taskkill /F /T on Windows, killpg elsewhere) before collecting output.
failures.prevention_notes: A subprocess timeout must kill the process tree, not the shell; the test bounds the measured duration so a regression shows on every platform.

failures.title: A version-file test compared a POSIX path string on Windows
failures.how_detected: CI on PR #2 (windows-latest), read by test name
failures.root_cause: write_omni_version_file stores str(Path(source)), which Windows renders with backslashes; the test asserted the POSIX literal.
failures.prevention_notes: Compare paths through pathlib in tests; CI runs three operating systems for exactly this.

failures.title: omni adopt --include-cli into an empty target always exited 1
failures.symptom: The adopt-loop CI script died at the adopt step: omni adopt --target <empty dir> --include-cli reported the three .ai/graph-viewer files as 'skip existing' and returned 1, although the adoption had copied everything.
failures.how_detected: the adopt-loop CI script and test (REQ-041), by exit code
failures.root_cause: ADOPTION_CLI_FILES lists .ai/graph-viewer/viewer.html, 3d-force-graph.min.js and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, which are already present once .ai is copied whole in the same run; copy_adoption_path then saw them as pre-existing and the skip was counted as a failure. Present since REQ-021; never seen because adopt had only been run into targets that already carried .ai.
failures.fix_summary: run_adopt tracks the directories it copied in the same run and reports a nested path as copied with its directory; targets that already had .ai keep the previous behaviour.
failures.prevention_notes: The adopt loop now runs end to end in CI and in a test from an empty directory, so a regression in adopt itself fails the build.

failures.title: Every action in ci.yml was pinned by a mutable major tag
failures.symptom: Code scanning on upstream OmniEngineering PR #3 raised four 'Action actions/checkout pinned to a mutable ref (v5)' notes (arbiter/supply.unpinned-action) on .github/workflows/ci.yml; the same finding was an open entry (FAIL-046) in the vendored Arbiter's ledger.
failures.how_detected: code scanning on upstream OmniEngineering PR #3 (Arbiter SARIF)
failures.root_cause: The workflow referenced actions/checkout@v5, actions/setup-python@v5, actions/cache@v4 and github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3 by major tag; a tag can be moved, so the workflow ran whatever the tag pointed at on the day.
failures.fix_summary: Every uses: line names the tag's commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment (checkout fbc6f399, setup-python a26af69b, cache 0057852b, upload-sarif 9f759ee6, resolved with git ls-remote --tags).
failures.no_test_reason: A workflow file has no unit test; Arbiter's supply.unpinned-action rule in the self-gate is the check that catches a return to tags.
failures.prevention_notes: Arbiter's supply-chain probe reports a mutable action ref on every gate run; the SARIF upload makes it a code-scanning alert.

failures.title: History-layer test teardown raced git's detached auto-gc on macOS CI
failures.symptom: CI (macos-latest, Python 3.10) on pull request #6: ERROR in test_graph_layers.TestHistoryLayer.test_a_squash_commit_without_an_id_is_tied_to_the_requirement_its_changelog_entry_records: TemporaryDirectory cleanup raised OSError Errno 66 Directory not empty: 'pack'. The same test passed on the previous head and on every other cell.
failures.how_detected: CI on pull request #6, read by test name
failures.root_cause: The test commits several times into a temporary repository; git may detach an automatic gc that writes into .git/objects/pack after the commit returns, so shutil.rmtree listed the pack directory, git added a file, and rmdir failed.
failures.fix_summary: Every temporary repository in the history-layer tests sets gc.auto 0 right after git init, so no background process writes into the directory the test removes.
failures.no_test_reason: The defect is a timing race in test teardown; the fix removes the background process rather than asserting on it.
failures.prevention_notes: A test that creates a git repository and removes it disables auto-gc; the macOS cell is the control that showed the race.

failures.title: Lineage test teardown raced git's detached auto-gc on macOS CI (recurrence of FAIL-017 in a fixture subclass)
failures.symptom: CI (macos-latest, Python 3.10) on the push run for upstream OmniEngineering branch arbiter at 3d1a17d: ERROR in test_lineage.TestLineage.test_a_walk_terminates_on_a_cycle: TemporaryDirectory cleanup raised OSError Errno 66 Directory not empty: 'objects'. The same cell passed on the pull-request run of the same commit.
failures.how_detected: CI on the upstream branch, read by test name; the twin job on the pull-request run passed
failures.root_cause: FAIL-017 disabled auto-gc in the three history-layer tests that call git init themselves, but TestLineage (and every other subclass of the shared Fixture in tests/test_graph_layers.py) commits into its own temporary repository through Fixture.git without that setting, so git could still detach a gc that writes under .git/objects after the commit returns, racing shutil.rmtree in teardown.
failures.fix_summary: Fixture.git passes -c gc.auto=0 on every git invocation, so every fixture repository (layers, lineage, findings, benchmark, vendored-and-blame) runs without a background gc; the fix lives in the one helper every subclass uses instead of in each test.
failures.no_test_reason: A timing race in test teardown; the fix removes the background process rather than asserting on it, as for FAIL-017.
failures.prevention_notes: A test that creates and removes a git repository runs git with auto-gc off; doing it in the shared helper means a new subclass cannot forget it.
